mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid engine typically costs between £7,500 and £11,000 for a rebuilt unit fitted by a specialist. Used engines start from around £3,500 supply-only.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of crankshaft failure in a Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning is a knocking noise from the engine, particularly noticeable on cold start-up, which often worsens under load.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical 2013-2017 Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid retains significant value (£12,000-£25,000 depending on condition and mileage), so a rebuilt engine at £7,500-£11,000 fitted is usually a sound investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full engine replacement typically takes 3-7 days depending on the workshop's schedule and parts availability.

mainEntity.name: What causes Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid engine failure?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 306DT engine in the SDV6 Hybrid is prone to two primary failure modes: crankshaft bearing fatigue (tin-aluminium coating failure) and timing chain tensioner wear.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the SDV6 Hybrid and the standard SDV6?

acceptedAnswer.text: The SDV6 Hybrid pairs the same 3.0-litre 306DT diesel engine with a 35kW electric motor, boosting combined output to 340-349hp versus 258-292hp for the standard SDV6.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid's 306DT engine shares the fundamental architecture of the broader SDV6 family, with hybrid-specific complexities adding another layer of potential failure points. Replacement demand for this variant is driven primarily by catastrophic crankshaft failure and, less frequently, timing chain issues. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Crankshaft Bearing Failure - Why the Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid 306DT Fails Catastrophically
problems.rootCause: The original tin-aluminium bearing coating on the 306DT engine family is prone to fatigue, leading to bearing failure and crankshaft damage. This often occurs without warning, though a cold-start knock may be audible in the weeks before failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt 306DT with upgraded crankshaft and bearings, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The only viable option if crankshaft has failed or bearings have spun

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2013-2017 Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid with 60,000-100,000 miles is valued between £12,000 and £25,000 depending on condition and spec [THIRD-PARTY - Parkers/Auto Trader market observation]. With replacement cost typically under £11,000 fitted through a specialist, the investment is usually justified relative to vehicle value for most examples. However, if the vehicle has covered over 120,000 miles or shows significant other wear, weigh the replacement cost against the car's overall condition and consider scrap value.
problems.recommendation: Crankshaft failure on an SDV6 Hybrid is typically sudden and without warning. If you hear a knocking noise on cold start-up, have the engine inspected immediately. If the engine has already failed, a rebuilt unit with a revised crankshaft and heavy-duty bearings is the most cost-effective long-term solution. Choose a specialist with experience on the SDV6 hybrid system - the electric motor integration adds complexity.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 306DT Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - The Preventable Failure on the Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid
problems.rootCause: The original timing chain tensioners on the 306DT engine family are prone to wear, allowing the chain to stretch and eventually jump timing. This can lead to valve-to-piston contact and catastrophic engine failure if not addressed promptly.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chains, tensioners and guides with upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early with rattle on start-up; prevents catastrophic failure

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of rebuilt 306DT with upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has failed and engine is damaged; or high-mileage engine with multiple issues

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above, a typical SDV6 Hybrid retains sufficient value to justify either repair or replacement. For a vehicle worth £15,000-£25,000, a preventative timing chain replacement at £1,800-£2,800 is excellent value if caught early. If the engine has already failed, replacement is the only viable path.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattle on cold start-up from your Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid, have the timing chain inspected immediately - catching it early could save you thousands. If the engine has already failed or is showing multiple issues, a rebuilt unit with upgraded components offers the best long-term reliability. The hybrid system does not affect the timing chain repair procedure significantly, but specialist experience with the SDV6 platform is essential.

items.question: What causes Range Rover Sport SDV6 Hybrid engine failure?
items.answer: The 306DT engine in the SDV6 Hybrid is prone to two primary failure modes: crankshaft bearing fatigue (tin-aluminium coating failure) and timing chain tensioner wear.

Hybrid system components can also fail independently but are less common
Regular servicing and early attention to warning signs are critical
